sections.title: What does it mean?
sections.content: Hungarian spelling is highly regular. Letters usually represent the same sounds wherever they appear. Some Hungarian letters are written with two or three characters, but they still count as one letter.

sections.title: How does it work?
sections.content: Hungarian has short and long vowels. Long vowels are marked with an acute accent, or with a double acute for *ő* and *ű*. Hungarian also has letters written with two or three characters, such as *sz*, *cs*, *gy*, *ny* and *zs*.

sections.title: Why does it look like this?
sections.content: The accent marks are part of the spelling. They are not decoration, and they can distinguish different sounds and words. The same principle applies to letter combinations: *sz* is one Hungarian letter, not the English sounds s and z separately.
English speakers often read Hungarian *s* like English s. Do not: Hungarian *s* is pronounced like English sh, while Hungarian *sz* is pronounced like English s in see.
